clue.text: Enlarge head of deltoid by endless exercise system

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, here of deltoid
without its ends, so the exercise word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Pilates is a system of exercises for core strength

explanation.surface: A gym instruction: build up your shoulder muscle by following a full exercise regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to widen or make larger, as a pupil or blood vessel does.

clue.text: Work out final bit of coded extract

indicators.note: the final bit of a word is its last letter, here of coded

parts.note: to educe is to draw out or extract

explanation.surface: A codebreaker deciphers the last part of an encrypted passage.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a conclusion by reasoning, i.e. to figure something out.

clue.text: Record finding yellow flightless bird in uncontrollable flow of words

parts.note: a log is a record, as a ship's log
or is gold or yellow in heraldry
the rhea is a large flightless bird of South America

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher logs a yellow flightless bird amid a torrent of chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: Note the American-style spelling, without the second O found in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical and literary term for excessive, compulsive talkativeness.

clue.text: Water secreted in nearly all treated timber support

indicators.note: secreted means hidden away, so the water word is tucked inside
treated means processed, so the letters are worked into a new order
nearly all means the word timber loses its last letter

parts.note: ea is a dialect word for a river or stream

explanation.surface: Damp has got into almost every piece of treated wood in a support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timber support' looks like the definition, but 'timber' feeds the anagram; EA for water is an old dialect word for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal beam joining the feet of roof rafters, holding the structure together: a support.

clue.text: Opener hit back after cross over

indicators.note: after places the first piece ahead of the second in the answer
over signals that the word for cross is turned around

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix

indicators.note: back means the word for hit is read backwards

parts.note: to bonk is to hit, especially on the head

explanation.surface: Sounds like a cricket or boxing report: an opening batsman hits back after a cross ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' suggests a batsman, but it is the thing you turn to open a door. ROOD is an old word for the Cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the handle you turn is what opens a door.

clue.text: Run out of pigment for groove

indicators.note: out of means the run letter is taken away from the pigment word

parts.note: ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A painter runs out of colour for a channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The oche is the line behind which darts players stand; originally it could be a groove in the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The darts throwing line, once marked as a groove or ridge on a pub floor.

clue.text: Voicing regret with hurtful remark? That's codswallop!

indicators.note: voicing means saying out loud, so a word is given by its sound

parts.note: to rue is to regret
a barb is a cutting, wounding remark

explanation.surface: Someone expresses sorrow along with a jibe, and is told it is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for nonsense; also the murmur actors make to sound like a crowd talking.

clue.text: Encourage fatty to change top

indicators.note: change top means the opening letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a pudge is a short fat person

explanation.surface: Urging an overweight person to swap their shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter P of PUDGE is replaced by N; the clue does not say which letter comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle prod: to push or prompt someone along toward doing something.

clue.text: Dark-red ruby dug out around central section of Kenya

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters wrap round the Kenyan letter
out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
the central section is the middle letter of Kenya

explanation.surface: A ruby gem has been mined around the heart of Kenya.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour named after the red wine of the French region: a deep purplish red.

clue.text: Follow on to bend in fairway

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: Golf advice: follow through to the bend in the fairway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' as LEG is a cricket term: the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf hole whose fairway turns sharply partway along is called by this name, from the angle of a hound's hind limb.

clue.text: Take responsibility for repairing old hurdles

indicators.note: repairing means putting the pieces back together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A groundsman accepts the job of mending battered old hurdles.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a burden or duty is to carry it on your back, hence accepting responsibility.

clue.text: Tidal barrier starts to strengthen estuarine area's defence

indicators.note: the starts are the first letters of strengthen, estuarine and area's

parts.note: a wall is a defensive barrier

explanation.surface: Engineers begin shoring up an estuary's flood defences.
explanation.definitionFit: An embankment built to hold back the sea is a barrier against the tide.

clue.text: Restricted group in centre start to demonstrate

indicators.note: in places the group word inside the word for centre

parts.note: the core is the centre of something
a set is a group

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of demonstrate

explanation.surface: A political picture: a central faction is barred from starting a demonstration.
explanation.definitionFit: Laced into a tight undergarment, someone is confined or constrained; figuratively, restricted.

clue.text: River craft's a beaut following refit

indicators.note: a refit rebuilds something, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: After a refit the old riverboat looks lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: French for boat; in English it names a light flat-bottomed riverboat used in Canada and Louisiana.

clue.text: Dietary requirement for adolescent, they say

indicators.note: they say signals a word given by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: pro means for, and a teen is an adolescent

explanation.surface: A nutrition tip aimed at teenagers.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrient found in meat, eggs and beans that the body needs for growth: a dietary essential.

clue.text: Rogue had mower fixed en route to place of origin

definitions.text: en route to place of origin

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means wild or out of control, so the letters run wild

parts.note: bound means fixed or tied fast

explanation.surface: A villain repaired the lawnmower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like a noun for a villain but is the anagram signal; 'fixed' looks like the anagram signal but supplies BOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading for home: travelling back towards where you started from.

clue.text: Translation of a blue novel, not English, does not inspire affection

indicators.note: a translation renders words anew, so the letters are reworked
not means the English letter is left out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A racy foreign novel loses its appeal once translated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not English' removes one E from A BLUE NOVEL before the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that cannot be loved fails to stir any fondness in people.

clue.text: Group, including core of nutters, occupied building

indicators.note: including means the group word holds the core letters inside it

parts.note: a squad is a group or team

indicators.note: the core is the middle three letters of nutters

explanation.surface: A gang with some cranks at its heart took over an empty block.
explanation.definitionFit: Squatters move into an empty house without permission, so they occupied the building.

clue.text: Muscle's arterial construction beginning to lose shape

parts.note: quad is short for quadriceps, the thigh muscle

indicators.note: construction means the letters are built into a new order
the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of lose

explanation.surface: A medical note: the artery feeding a muscle starts to lose its form.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided plane figure is a geometric shape, such as a square or kite.

clue.text: Reckless driver smashed a door hard against edge of gutter

indicators.note: smashed means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: the edge here is the first letter of gutter

explanation.surface: A crash: a car door slammed against the kerb.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist who hogs the road, driving selfishly and dangerously.

clue.text: Motorists steer round old animal

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

indicators.note: round means the steering word goes around the old letter

parts.note: to con a ship is to direct its steering

explanation.surface: Drivers swerve to avoid an old creature on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringtailed masked North American mammal is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Bard entreats with passion intrinsically

indicators.note: intrinsically means within, so the letters are found inside these words

explanation.surface: Shakespeare pleads fervently.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate and fervent; full of burning feeling.

clue.text: Slash, perhaps, as one cutting costs

definitions.meaning: Slash, the Guns N' Roses lead guitarist, is an example of a rock guitar player, axe being slang for guitar
a person who chops budgets ruthlessly

explanation.surface: A finance boss is a slasher, a cost-cutter.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a guitarist (an axe is a guitar), and also a ruthless cutter of spending.

clue.text: Story arising about old lady's message

indicators.note: about means the reversed story word goes around the mother word
arising in a down clue means the word for story is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a lie is a story, a fib
ma is mum, one's old lady

explanation.surface: A tale emerges concerning a mother's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic message sent over the internet.

clue.text: Find Iceland's head of cod-fishery in port

indicators.note: in places the Iceland and cod pieces inside the port

parts.note: Dover is an English Channel port
IS is the international code for Iceland

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of cod-fishery

explanation.surface: Looking for the boss of an Icelandic cod fishery at a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: DOVER is a ferry port in Kent on the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to come upon or detect something, as in locating something lost.

clue.text: Piercing wail

definitions.meaning: sharp or cutting, as a blade or a wind
to lament loudly over the dead

explanation.surface: A shrill, piercing cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp, as an edge or wind; and as a verb, to lament in a high cry, especially at an Irish funeral.

clue.text: Is her art nouveau comparatively worthless?

indicators.note: nouveau means new, so the letters are made new by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Asking whether a woman's Art Nouveau work is of lesser value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art nouveau' reads as the decorative style, but 'nouveau' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative of the slang adjective for rubbishy or tasteless, so more worthless.

clue.text: By the middle of session card game gets serious

indicators.note: the middle letter of session, its fourth of seven

parts.note: ombre is an old Spanish card game for three players

explanation.surface: Halfway through a session the card game takes a grave turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and gloomy in mood, a near synonym of serious or solemn.

clue.text: With training idle Northern git becomes industrious

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the letters are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: With some training even a lazy northern lout becomes hard-working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'git' is British slang for an unpleasant or foolish person.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-working and painstaking: a straight synonym of industrious.

clue.text: Kind entrepreneur nurtures apprentice

indicators.note: nurtures means holds and protects, so the letters sit within these two words

explanation.surface: A generous businessman takes a trainee under his wing.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind someone as an apprentice by a contract called an indenture; apprentice here is a verb.
